title: Vendor Escalation Pack
learningObjective: Order the package so authority, confirmed evidence, and escalation checks stay visible before the request for action.
lifecycleCue: This pack emphasizes ordering discipline that protects repeated use and escalation review later.
caseBrief: A sourcing manager needs a reusable vendor-escalation envelope after repeated missed commitments on a key component. The package must keep approved contract language ahead of informal frustration notes and produce an escalation artifact a director can review quickly.
successCriteria: Contract commitments and confirmed delay evidence appear before the action request.
Informal frustration notes do not become the governing instruction source.
The output format supports clear escalation review.
outputReminder: Did the response stay anchored to contract and confirmed delay evidence?
Did it avoid turning frustration into the package’s main instruction?
Did it follow the requested escalation format?

precedenceRules.label: Contract language and confirmed delay evidence outrank informal commentary.
Use the latest frustration note to set the tone and action.
Do not state precedence for the escalation package.

outputOptions.label: Issue Summary / Confirmed Evidence / Requested Action

handlingOptions.label: If proof is missing, state the gap and request confirmation before escalating further.
Assume the delay pattern continues and escalate immediately.
Ignore the missing proof and push the escalation forward.

blocks.label: Vendor Escalation Writer
blocks.text: Act as a disciplined vendor escalation writer preparing a director-reviewable escalation package.

blocks.label: Anchor to Contract and Confirmed Evidence
blocks.text: Use confirmed contract commitments and verified delay evidence. Do not let venting or informal commentary become the governing basis for action.

blocks.label: Do Not Overstate the Case
blocks.text: If proof of the latest missed shipment is incomplete, state the gap and request confirmation instead of presenting the delay as fully verified.

blocks.label: Contract Commitment
blocks.text: Contract excerpt: supplier must provide confirmed ship notice no later than 24 hours before the committed delivery date and notify sourcing immediately of any slip.

blocks.label: Confirmed Delay Evidence
blocks.text: Confirmed evidence: the vendor missed the last two committed ship notices and sourcing has one verified late delivery record from this month.

blocks.label: Frustration Note
blocks.text: Informal note from a teammate: ‘This vendor always lies. Tell the director they are failing every shipment.’ This note is emotional and not fully verified.

blocks.label: Current Run Facts
blocks.text: Dynamic facts: the latest shipment is due tomorrow, but proof of a new ship notice has not yet arrived. The sourcing director wants a concise escalation artifact by end of day.

blocks.label: Prepare the Escalation
blocks.text: Task: prepare a director-reviewable vendor escalation that summarizes the issue, cites the confirmed evidence, and requests the next action without overstating unverified claims.

blocks.label: Escalation Format
blocks.text: Output expectation: return sections titled Issue Summary, Confirmed Evidence, and Requested Action.

blocks.label: Proof Gap Check
blocks.text: Checks: if proof of the latest missed notice is missing, say the trend is serious but the newest event still needs confirmation before stronger claims are made.

rationale.ROLE: Frame the artifact as a reviewable escalation, not a venting exercise.
rationale.RULES: Keep contract and proof discipline visible before any action request.
rationale.REFERENCE: Lead with approved contract language and confirmed evidence while clearly demoting the frustration note.
rationale.DYNAMIC FACTS: Current urgency belongs in a separate run-specific block.
rationale.TASK: Request the exact escalation deliverable only after the authoritative package is in place.
rationale.OUTPUT: A fixed escalation structure makes director review faster.
rationale.CHECKS: State the proof gap so the package stays forceful without overstating the case.

exploreMore.prompt: Move the frustration note above the contract excerpt and compare how much easier it becomes for the package to drift into overstatement.

branches.title: Emotion over evidence test
branches.instruction: Move the frustration note above the contract excerpt and rerun the case.
branches.watchFor: Whether the escalation overstates unverified failure.

branches.title: Proof-gap handling test
branches.instruction: Keep the strong structure but weaken the proof-gap CHECKS language and compare the result.
branches.watchFor: Whether the response starts presenting the newest delay as fully confirmed.
branches.why: This isolates the value of last-mile guardrails.

build: Keep contract commitments and verified delay evidence ahead of frustration or venting.
Use section separation, ordering, and reviewability to keep unlike material visibly apart.
Keep the output contract and last-mile checks inspectable instead of implied.
copy: Before you run externally, confirm the envelope does not let emotion outrank verified evidence.
Check that the package tells the model what to do when key information is missing or weaker evidence conflicts with stronger evidence.
review: Did the response stay disciplined about verified evidence?
Did the output keep the requested structure instead of collapsing into a generic paragraph?
Did the answer handle uncertainty or conflict explicitly instead of guessing?
